metadata.title: Main findings and implications for education policies in Europe

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document summarizes results from ICILS 2013, which surveyed and assessed grade 8 students in 21 education systems (including 9 EU countries). The report describes an international, multi-stage school/student sampling design (students nested in schools and education systems), but it does not specify the exact weight variables or replicate-weight method used in the analyses summarized here. For ICILS analyses, analysts working with the international database should apply the provided student sampling weights and, where available, replicate weights to obtain correct standard errors under the complex survey design. Because this is a policy-oriented synthesis rather than a methods chapter, the specific weight variable names and replication procedure are not reported in the excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This policy synthesis does not report the technical details of plausible value (PV) generation/combining or the missing-data handling strategy used in the underlying ICILS international analyses. While ICILS reports achievement on a proficiency scale, the excerpt does not describe whether PVs were used, how they were combined, or what missing-data procedure was applied. Therefore, the missing-data handling is treated as a reporting gap for this document excerpt.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The excerpt states that ICILS 2013 gathered data from almost 60,000 grade 8 students in more than 3,300 schools across 21 education systems, with main fieldwork carried out in 2013. It does not specify additional analytic exclusions (e.g., missing questionnaire/assessment records, specific task completion thresholds, or sub-sampling rules) for the policy results presented in this document. It also notes that ICILS covered two regions of Canada and one region in Argentina, and that results for these regions are not included in this paper.

data.outcome_summary: ICILS 2013 is an international large-scale assessment of computer and information literacy (CIL) for grade 8 students (average age 13.5), with main fieldwork in 2013. The policy document reports results from nearly 60,000 students in 3,300+ schools across 21 education systems, including 9 EU countries, and uses a CIL achievement scale with a mean of 500 points (equally weighted national samples) divided into proficiency levels (below level 1 through level 4). The report also draws on student, teacher, and school questionnaires to describe computer use, attitudes, teacher ICT self-efficacy, and the pedagogical embedding of ICT. Key benchmarks are expressed as shares of students at low proficiency (e.g., 15–45% in participating EU countries) and very high proficiency (less than 5% in all participating EU countries). The document is a synthesis for EU policy dialogue and does not provide the technical PV/missing-data/weighting procedures used in the underlying international analyses.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a policy synthesis of ICILS 2013 results rather than an empirical ML study with a specified predictive modeling pipeline. As a result, it does not report model training algorithms, PV-combining procedures, missing-data handling, or per-country analytic sample sizes needed for ML-method extraction. The excerpt also does not provide the technical details required to populate ML-specific fields (e.g., primary algorithm, performance metrics) or to enumerate conceptual predictors used in a multivariable predictive model.
